trust_decision.summary: The API token is a secret; whether it may be sent to a URL is decided by that URL's provenance. A URL supplied by automatically discovered project configuration (cwd or any parent) is untrusted, so an unscoped key (WLC_KEY or --key) may not be paired with it; a URL pinned by --url/WLC_URL, by an explicit --config, by the user's own XDG/APPDATA config, or a URL-scoped [keys] entry stays allowed. Enforced in WeblateConfig.get_url_key()/validate_url_key().

landing_point.why: get_url_key() is the only place the API key is paired with a URL (cli_url/WLC_URL/config url, then cli_key/WLC_KEY/keys[url]); a reader of 'wlc may disclose API tokens to project-configured URLs' lands here first, and the published fix's guard lands here too.

fix_sites.entry_point: WeblateConfig.load() — wlc CLI discovery and the library call WeblateConfig.load(path)
fix_sites.module_kind: config loader (provenance tracking of the URL source)

fix_sites.entry_point: WeblateConfig.load() — explicit --config vs user XDG config vs discovered project config
WeblateConfig.get_url_key() / validate_url_key(), reached by wlc.Weblate(config=...) and by every CLI subcommand
wlc console script (all subcommands) through wlc.main.parse_settings()

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The README advertises repository-provided project configuration plus an injected WLC_KEY as a supported CI workflow (README.md:75-77), so a library-level guard in the shared get_url_key() — which also affects embedders who constructed their own WeblateConfig — can be argued to be beyond the advisory's CLI scenario.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Pairing an explicitly chosen config URL with WLC_KEY must keep working (explicit --config and the XDG/APPDATA user config), as must WLC_KEY with no config-supplied URL (default API_URL) and a project-config URL with a matching URL-scoped [keys] entry. A fix that refuses the env/CLI key whenever any config file supplied the URL, or whenever a project config file exists, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: key from env WLC_KEY vs key from CLI --key
key from the URL-scoped [keys] section (must stay allowed with project config)
URL from discovered project config named .weblate, .weblate.ini or weblate.ini, in cwd or in any parent directory
URL pinned by --url or WLC_URL (must stay allowed)
URL from explicit --config or from XDG/APPDATA user config (must stay allowed)
no URL configured at all, so the default API_URL is used

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an env-selected config discovery (e.g. WLC_CONFIG, or honouring XDG_CONFIG_HOME/paths for a second config name) added to find_config()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: 2.0.0 already introduced env-var configuration (WLC_URL/WLC_KEY) and find_config() already branches on APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA, so a maintainer adding one more discovery source is natural — and it would need the same URL-provenance tag or it silently trusts a repo-chosen path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a profile/defaults merge route, e.g. a [weblate:<profile>] section or a --profile option merging url into the active section
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: set_defaults() already writes url/retries/timeout into the active section and the README documents a precedence chain, so a merge/profile layer is a plausible next feature and would bypass _config_url_source.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a --key-file or --env-file CLI option that fills cli_key/cli_url from a project-supplied file
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the CLI already carries --key/--url, the project previously had to reject an unscoped 'key' in settings (wlc/config.py:96-99), and 2.0.0 added the WLC_KEY secret plumbing; a file-based secret option would inherit exactly the same unscoped-key problem.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a convenience constructor such as Weblate.from_config()/from_env() that builds url+key without calling validate_url_key()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the constructor already has two branches (config object vs explicit key/url), so a third convenience entry is idiomatic for this codebase and would silently reopen the sink.

O9_family: CWE-200 exposure of sensitive information / CWE-349 acceptance of extraneous untrusted data with trusted data: an untrusted configuration source selects the destination of a trusted API token

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools build backend; CI uses uv (`uv sync --all-extras --dev`, `uv run py.test --cov=wlc tests`); pytest + pytest-cov + responses
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_config.py (config resolution, file discovery, precedence) and tests/test_main.py::TestSettings (CLI settings, --config, WLC_KEY/WLC_URL, APPDATA config); HTTP is mocked with the `responses` library against tests/test_data fixtures, so the affected behaviour needs no network.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Guard in the CLI handler only: raise whenever find_project_config() returns a file and WLC_KEY/--key is set — leaves Weblate(config=...) open and breaks explicit --config, XDG user config and the project-config + WLC_URL / scoped-[keys] cases.

out_of_scope_notes: Outside the advisory's property (project configuration): a URL supplied by the user's own XDG/APPDATA config can still be paired with WLC_KEY after the fix (wlc/config.py:51-66, 88-92), and pinned tests rely on that (tests/test_main.py:196-205).

Outside the advisory's property: wlc.main(settings=...) injects URL values through config.set() (wlc/main.py:929-933) without ever setting a URL provenance, so a caller-supplied URL plus WLC_KEY bypasses the new guard; the caller, not the repository, chose it.

Already hardened by earlier advisories and not part of this sink: cross-origin request URLs are rejected (wlc/client.py:119-126), redirects are refused (wlc/client.py:275) and the Authorization header is redacted from debug logs (wlc/http_debug.py:23-28).
